findings.claim: The new ordinary delivery protocol fixes pending-event erasure, but its recovery promises still describe a stronger guarantee than the actual rules. This is a specification/documentation defect; the disclosed choice to abandon an old event on Issue rotation is not itself being presented as an undisclosed implementation bug.

If that event was a red warning and the current state has recovered to fresh, W0 resets da_bao to unknown and cho_bao to null; the new Issue receives a fresh nhip_tim_gian_doan, never the old red state. The same passage and allocation paragraph also promise rule (c) for every missing/unreadable heartbeat, although rule (a) wins when current S is warning. Scan covered I6, W0/W1/allocation, notification priority, section 10, deviations 10/12, runbook 2a/4a and the r3 changelog.

manifestations.claim: Row 94 mutates the single shared m16 validator. In n8_truoc_khung_dau it rejects the generated heartbeat before the first PATCH. The next run therefore reads vang (or a preserved old body), not the promised nhip_tim_sai_mien:dong_den:m16 from a newly written heartbeat. The designated round-2 read observation is unreachable under the required writer precheck.

Row 95 writes a full Unicode/long diagnostic instead of its head. The shared writer validator rejects it at m9 before PATCH; the promised second-run m9 readback is likewise unreachable. Both rows must observe the rejection at the first write boundary, not require an invalid heartbeat to have been persisted.

Row 99 targets n15_han_cuoi_danh_gia: final T7 starts at 599, needs 2s, timeout is clamped to 1. At 600 the GET has timed out and its mandatory retry/wait precheck already observes exhausted time. Removing only the final evaluation check need not yield fresh; a conforming implementation still returns S1. The existing CPU-after-success case n15_phan_tich_qua_han is a discriminating target.

Row 106 targets W8 needing 2s with only 1s left. The clamped transport timeout independently makes W8 incomplete and returns rc3. Dropping its completion clock check does not turn that failure into the promised rc1. A successful HTTP response followed by parsing/readback work crossing the deadline isolates this check.

Acceptance 2 adds kiem_nhip_tim to the statement that every injected primitive exception must never produce fresh, while also requiring the W0 fault to trigger notification rule (c). A one-shot W0 validator failure followed by valid audit inputs leaves S=fresh and emits the gap event: heartbeat parsing is not an S1 cause. If the monkeypatch throws on every call, the writer precheck also fails, giving zero POSTs rather than row115's required one. Scope the injection and distinguish audit state from heartbeat/delivery state.

The root heartbeat closed-key-set check (nhip_tim_tap_khoa) is outside m1..m33 and has no dedicated mutant in rows1..115. Row61 mutates m conditions; m17/m26 protect nested event keys only. Adding one extra root key leaves every field predicate unchanged, so dropping this independent guard is a distinguishable missing mutation, not an equivalent case.

T2's expired-receipt rejection has no dedicated mutant in the complete table. Removing this guard changes a receipt with expired=true and otherwise valid provided bytes from bien_nhan_het_han to dat; the listed digest/attempt/ZIP mutants do not mutate this check.

The R-class maximum of three redirects has an acceptance input but no dedicated mutant in the complete table. A four-redirect then valid-download transport distinguishes removal of this guard; GET retry-count row102 and evaluation-budget mutants are different checks.
